correctness.rationale: The proof verifies the polygon-resultant upper bound for all prices and all feasible nonnegative rates; shows attaining feasible rates and the exact spectral eigenvector; and establishes L(w*) - Lambda P positive semidefinite by an identity into weighted Cauchy--Schwarz deficit plus a square. Equality cases force all optimal weights uniquely, and the PSD nullity verifies spectral-gap multiplicity. The equality threshold and m=2 boundary are explicitly handled. The standalone exact checker passed 1360 rational parameter cases and 77488 rational factorization tests; finite checks are supplementary.

originality.rationale: The explicit optimal value and unique rate vector for arbitrary positive prices, with a square-root polygon inequality boundary and sharp gap-multiplicity transition, are more specific than the established general semidefinite and variance-unfolding methods. Sun et al. 2006 provide the full general framework, Göring et al. 2005 treat equal-price stars, and Farhadi et al. 2022 treat tree embeddings and a distinct lambda-infinity star functional. Exact searches and full-text inspection found no explicit arbitrary-price star classification. Historical overlap risk persists, especially the Fiedler 1990 full text, which was unavailable; a negative search is not an originality certificate.
residual_risks: Fiedler 1990 complete text unavailable; a hidden arbitrary-cost tree/star formula cannot be excluded by its abstract.
Specialized historical weighted-star spectral-gap literature may use a different term for the price parameter; database and web searches cannot prove uniqueness.
The result is an explicit classification derived from general previously known SDP duality, not a new universal optimization principle.

value.rationale: The arbitrary independent positive rate prices form a natural full-dimensional network design input. The new closed-form result distinguishes a uniform optimum under a sharp square-root polygon condition from a unique nonuniform optimum beyond it, with exact gap and multiplicity. It is not a finite catalog or routine reparameterization of the one-cost example; the polygon-imbalance geometry affects every rate and provides a complete decision rule. No downstream theorem is required for this natural exact invariant.
